name: Indiana
tagline: Ohio River towns, canal locks, Brown County hills and the old roads to Lake Michigan.
intro: Indiana's byways follow the Ohio River and the old Whitewater Canal, cross the state on the National Road, the Lincoln Highway and the Michigan Road, and wind into the Brown County hills. This chapter follows the Indiana Byway Program of the Indiana Department of Transportation, where each byway is designated by an order of the INDOT Commissioner with the Lieutenant Governor's concurrence. Three of the nine are also National Scenic Byways, and the Whitewater Canal byway carries three loop routes that were added three years after the main road.

members.name: Ohio River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Some 302 miles of Indiana road follow the Ohio River across thirteen hilly counties, linking old river towns with the Devonian fossil beds at the Falls of the Ohio, Evansville and the communal-era village of New Harmony.

members.name: Historic National Road
members.blurb: US 40 carries most of the old National Road 156 miles across Indiana, from Richmond and the Whitewater River gorge through Indianapolis to Terre Haute, past pike towns, farmland and a tollhouse saved at Plainfield.

members.name: Indiana's Historic Pathways
members.blurb: A Y of two old highways, US 50 from Lawrenceburg and US 150 from Clarksville, joins and runs west to Vincennes near the line of the Buffalo Trace, passing Paoli's courthouse square and the East Fork White River at Shoals.

members.name: Wabash River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A short river road in Tippecanoe County, starting at Ross Hills County Park and following South and North River Roads up the Wabash past the site of Fort Ouiatenon to I-65 near Prophetstown State Park.

members.name: Whitewater Canal Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The byway follows the old canal line down the Whitewater valley from Hagerstown to Lawrenceburg by way of Connersville and Metamora, where restored canal water still turns a grain mill and crosses Duck Creek on a rebuilt wooden aqueduct.

members.name: Whitewater Canal Scenic Byway Loop Routes
members.blurb: Added in 2011, three side loops leave the canal byway: one east to Richmond and back through Liberty, one by way of Oldenburg to Batesville and St. Leon, and one from Lawrenceburg through Aurora, Milan and Sunman.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Historic Michigan Road Byway
members.blurb: Commissioned in the 1820s as Indiana's first state road, the Michigan Road still runs from Madison on the Ohio through Greensburg, Indianapolis and Logansport to South Bend and Michigan City on Lake Michigan.

members.name: Lincoln Highway Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Two alignments of Carl Fisher's coast-to-coast highway cross northern Indiana, the 1913 road through Goshen, Elkhart, South Bend and La Porte and the 1928 road through Warsaw and Plymouth, meeting at Valparaiso.

members.name: Hoosier Hills State Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Some 83 miles from Belleville on US 40 to US 50 west of Brownstown, by Martinsville's courthouse square into Brown County, where SR 135 winds through Bean Blossom, Nashville and Story along Brown County State Park.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.
